first.rationale: Verify promotional-pricing evidence because competitor entry pricing creates an immediate, high-consequence SMB acquisition risk, while sustainable qualified revenue requires confirming quality, retention, and margin effects rather than relying on acquisition lift alone. Verify onboarding evidence because completion and activation are both declining and it is the strongest alternative use of the single slot. Pending verification, run a narrowly targeted SMB pricing test with qualified-revenue, retention, and discount/margin guardrails.

mid.rationale: Run the shortened-onboarding experiment. Its archived record directly supports sustainable value: completion increased 13%, time-to-value fell 2.1 days, and 30-day retention increased 3%. This addresses the current declines in both onboarding completion and activation. Do not use promotional pricing this cycle: although it raised qualified revenue initially, its 12% 30-day retention decline makes it unsuitable for the primary objective of sustainable long-term qualified revenue.

final2.rationale: Maintain the shortened-onboarding experiment. The verified result improves completion, time-to-value, and 30-day retention, directly supporting sustainable qualified revenue amid declining activation and completion. The competitor's deeper cut makes the SMB threat more urgent, but the only verified pricing evidence showed a 12% retention decline after targeted discounts; escalating discounting would risk exchanging near-term saves or signups for lower-value, less durable cohorts. Price-sensitive churn risk remains material and should be monitored, but it does not overturn the available evidence for the single experiment slot.
